rationale: D5 (#961): C++ has no nested function definition, so a `function_definition` inside a function body is ill-formed and is instead the one thing that shape genuinely is — a local variable written with direct-initialization parentheses (`T name(args);` and `T name(args) { }` are ambiguous to a parser with no symbol table, and tree-sitter-cpp resolves toward the function reading). 619 local variables were published as `function` symbols owned by the enclosing function over 554 real C++ files, so the graph's answer to 'what does this function contain' was a set of sibling functions. This was the THIRD guard of a family whose other two were already present: the field/variable branch refuses to publish inside a function (`insideFunction`), and `isMacroFunctionShape` refuses an untyped heading at file scope — neither reaches a node the grammar calls a `function_definition` that sits inside a body, which is exactly where the class lives. The second half is the CGD20 parity gap: a block-scoped `using X = Y;` / `typedef Y X;` is an execution artifact, and the C lane says so verbatim ('CGD20: function-local typedefs are execution artifacts (C-D1)') — 173 such aliases were published with the enclosing function as owner, half of them owned by a macro-heading function whose name is the literal heading text. The local VARIABLES still BIND as locals after the fix: dropping the binding would fabricate a read of an outer name of the same spelling, which `uses compute -> counter` at the end pins as the thing that must keep working.

expectSymbols.name: constructor
expectSymbols.note: `Handle(int)` is a real constructor and IS published — D5's gate is on a function DEFINITION nested in a body, not on constructors.

expectSymbols.name: local_type
expectSymbols.note: D5d, and the reason the CGD20 rule sits on the alias and is not a blanket 'nothing inside a function': a local CLASS has members, and they need an owner. The 38 legitimate function-owned symbols in the corpus are exactly these.

expectRelationships.note: D5c, the control for the gate being too broad: a real recursive CALL statement is still a call edge. The gate is on the DECLARATION, never on the callee — a version that keyed on 'a call inside a function' would delete every call in the language.
a member call on a local object.
the file-scope value read still resolves — the local bindings the D5 fix adds do not over-suppress outward resolution.
a local class's members are owned by it, which is the load-bearing reason local types are still published.

forbidSymbols.name: contents
forbidSymbols.note: D5a: `std::string contents("…");` is a local VARIABLE. Published as a `function` before the fix.

forbidSymbols.name: raw_stack
forbidSymbols.note: `std::vector<int> raw_stack(16);` — measured as `function "raw_stack" owner=GTEST_LOCK_EXCLUDED_(mutex_)` on the corpora.

forbidSymbols.name: left
forbidSymbols.note: D5b, the multi-declarator spelling — measured as `function "lhs" owner=FloatingPointLE` (gmock-gtest-all.cc:3109).

forbidSymbols.name: local_alias
forbidSymbols.note: D5e, CGD20 parity: a block-scoped alias is an execution artifact. The C lane states the rule; the C++ lane had no guard, so `type local_alias owner=compute` was published.

forbidSymbols.name: local_typedef
forbidSymbols.note: the same rule, the other C++ spelling.

forbidSymbols.name: lt
forbidSymbols.note: `local_type lt{5};` is BRACE initialization, which the grammar does not mistake for a definition — pinned so the fix is not over-broad enough to be about parens specifically.

forbidSymbols.name: doubled
forbidSymbols.note: `int doubled = compute(seed);` is a normal initialized declaration; pinned because it is the shape most at risk of being confused with a call.

forbidRelationships.note: D5e: the documented `contains` ontology is namespace→class/enum/alias, class→method/property/constructor, enum→member. `function -> block-scoped alias` is not in it.
D5a: the direct consequence — a local variable was a 'member' of the function that declared it.

D5 ROSTER, found while writing this fixture: a CONSTRUCTOR is not a callable value. `Handle(int)` defines a name that spells the class, and C++ never lets you call it unqualified — `Handle h(1)` is a construction, not a call. The roster is the resolution source for bare reads, so admitting it made the class name resolvable as a value and `Handle parent_handle(7);` published `uses Handle -> Handle` at confidence 1.0 — an edge asserting the class reads itself. The test is the name against the class it is declared in, which is exactly what a constructor is.
